module_title: Introduction to Solar Pumping for Dams

lessons.title: Overview of Dam Water Management and Pumping Needs
lessons.body:
A dam is not just a wall holding water. It is a storage system that must be managed daily. In Africa, many small dams serve irrigation, livestock, and domestic use. The water level drops in dry seasons, and you need to move water from the dam to where it is neededâoften uphill or over long distances. That is where pumping comes in.

Traditionally, farmers use diesel or petrol pumps. These are noisy, need fuel, and break down often. Fuel is expensive and sometimes unavailable in remote areas. Solar pumps offer a quiet, fuel-free alternative. But before choosing a pump, you must understand your dam's behavior. How much water enters during rains? How much is lost to evaporation and seepage? What is the daily demand for irrigation, cattle, or households?

For example, a 1-hectare vegetable plot in Kenya needs about 30,000 liters per day during peak season. A herd of 100 cattle drinks about 5,000 liters daily. If your dam is 500 meters from the plot and 10 meters higher, you need a pump that can push water that far and high. Solar pumps are rated by flow rate (liters per hour) and head (meters). You must match these to your dam's layout.

Also consider the dam's minimum water level. Never pump the dam dryâleave at least 30% for ecological and emergency use. A float switch can automatically stop the pump when water is too low. In summary, dam water management means balancing supply, demand, and pumping capacity. Solar pumping is a tool, but you must first know your numbers: volume needed, distance, elevation, and solar availability. This module will teach you how to gather those numbers and design a system that works for your dam.

lessons.title: Solar Pumping System Components and Configurations
lessons.body:
A solar pumping system has four main parts: solar panels, a controller or inverter, a pump, and piping. Sometimes you add a storage tank or batteries. Let's break each down.

Solar panels: These convert sunlight to electricity. You need enough panels to power the pump. A typical small system uses 4 to 8 panels of 250-300 watts each. Panels are mounted on a frame facing the sun. In Africa, tilt them toward the equator (north in southern Africa, south in northern Africa) at an angle equal to your latitude. For example, in Zambia (15Â°S), tilt panels 15Â° north.

Controller or inverter: This device matches the panel output to the pump. It also protects the pump from dry running and overvoltage. Many controllers have MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracking) to get the most power from panels. Some systems use a VFD (Variable Frequency Drive) for AC pumps.

Pump: Two main types: submersible (for deep wells or dams) and surface (for shallow water). Submersible pumps are placed inside the dam or a sump. Surface pumps sit on the bank and suck water. For dams, submersible is better because it avoids suction limits. Pump size is given in horsepower (HP) or watts. A 1 HP pump can lift about 10,000 liters per day to 10 meters head.

Piping: Use PVC or HDPE pipes. Size matters: a 32mm pipe carries less water than a 50mm pipe. Friction losses reduce flow, so keep pipes as short and straight as possible. Add a non-return valve to prevent backflow.

Configurations: Direct-coupled (panels power pump directly, no batteries) is cheapest and works for daytime irrigation. Battery-based systems store energy for night or cloudy days but cost more. For dams, direct-coupled with a storage tank is most common. You pump during sunny hours into a tank, then gravity-feed to fields. This reduces pump size and cost. Always include a float switch in the tank to stop the pump when full.

lessons.title: Advantages of Solar Pumps for Dam Applications
lessons.body:
Why choose solar over diesel or grid electricity for pumping from a dam? Here are the practical advantages, with real numbers.

Fuel savings: A diesel pump of 2 HP uses about 0.5 liters per hour. Running 6 hours daily costs 3 liters. At $1.20 per liter, that's $3.60 daily, or $1,314 per year. A solar pump of the same size costs about $1,200 upfront and has no fuel cost. It pays for itself in less than a year. After that, pumping is free.

Reliability: Diesel engines need maintenanceâoil changes, filters, spark plugs. They break down in remote areas where spare parts are scarce. Solar panels have no moving parts and last 20-25 years. Pumps last 5-10 years. Controllers last 5-8 years. So maintenance is minimal.

Environment: Diesel pumps emit CO2 and noise. They can leak fuel into the dam, harming fish and livestock. Solar pumps are silent and clean. This matters for community water supplies where children fetch water.

Scalability: You can start with a small solar pump and add panels later. For a dam, you might begin with a 500W system for 5,000 liters/day, then expand to 1,500W for 15,000 liters/day. Diesel pumps are harder to scaleâyou need a bigger engine.

Operation: Solar pumps work best when the sun shines, which is exactly when crops need water. You don't need to wake up early to start a diesel engine. The pump starts automatically at sunrise and stops at sunset. With a float switch, it stops when the tank is full.

Availability: Solar panels and controllers are now widely available in African cities like Nairobi, Accra, and Johannesburg. Prices have dropped 80% since 2010. A 300W panel costs about $150. Diesel, on the other hand, must be transported to remote dams, adding cost and risk.

In short, solar pumps save money, reduce labor, and protect the environment. For dam owners in Africa, they are often the best choice.

lessons.title: Site Assessment: Dam Location and Solar Resource
lessons.body:
Before buying any equipment, you must assess your site. This lesson shows you how to measure three things: dam layout, solar potential, and water quality.

Dam layout: Walk the dam and draw a simple map. Mark the water level at its lowest (dry season) and highest (rainy season). Measure the distance from the dam to the highest point where you need water. Use a tape measure or a GPS app on your phone. Also measure the elevation difference (head) using a clinometer or a smartphone level app. For example, if the dam is at 1,000m elevation and your tank is at 1,015m, head is 15m. Add friction loss: for every 100m of pipe, add 1m of head. So a 200m pipe adds 2m. Total head = 15 + 2 = 17m.

Solar resource: You need to know how much sun your site gets. Africa is luckyâmost areas get 4 to 6 peak sun hours per day. Peak sun hours are not the same as daylight hours. One peak sun hour = 1,000 watts per square meter. You can find maps from Global Solar Atlas or NASA POWER. For a quick check, use a solar pathfinder or a simple shadow test: at noon, a 1m stick should cast a shadow shorter than 1m in most of Africa. If your site is shaded by trees or hills, you must cut trees or move the panels. Panels must face the equator and be tilted at your latitude angle. For example, in Uganda (0Â° latitude), tilt 10Â° for rain runoff.

Water quality: Solar pumps can handle some sand and silt, but not mud. If your dam water is very muddy, use a settling tank or a floating intake filter. Test for salinity if you irrigateâtoo much salt harms crops. A simple EC meter costs $30. Also check for debris like leaves that can clog the pump. Install a screen around the intake.

Finally, check access: can you bring panels and pipes to the site? Is there security? Solar panels are stolen sometimes. Fence the array or mount panels on a roof. With these measurements, you can size your system accurately.

lessons.title: Water Demand Calculation for Dam Operations
lessons.body:
You cannot design a solar pump without knowing how much water you need. This lesson teaches you to calculate daily water demand for three common dam uses: irrigation, livestock, and domestic supply.

Irrigation: Water needs depend on crop, climate, and soil. A simple method is to use crop water requirement tables. For example, maize in a semi-arid area needs about 5-6 mm of water per day. One mm of water over 1 hectare = 10,000 liters. So 5 mm = 50,000 liters per hectare per day. If you have 0.5 hectares, demand is 25,000 liters/day. Vegetables like tomatoes need 6-7 mm. To be safe, add 20% for losses. So for 0.5 ha of tomatoes: 0.5 * 7 * 10,000 = 35,000 liters, plus 20% = 42,000 liters/day.

Livestock: Daily drinking water: cattle 40-50 liters, goats 5-10 liters, chickens 0.5 liters. For 50 cattle, 200 goats, and 500 chickens: (50*45) + (200*8) + (500*0.5) = 2,250 + 1,600 + 250 = 4,100 liters/day. Add 30% for cleaning and spillage = 5,330 liters/day.

Domestic: For a village of 100 people, each using 20 liters/day for drinking, cooking, and washing: 2,000 liters/day. Add 50% for livestock and gardens = 3,000 liters/day.

Total demand: Add all uses. If you have irrigation (42,000) + livestock (5,330) + domestic (3,000) = 50,330 liters/day. Round up to 55,000 liters/day for safety.

Now, match to pump: A solar pump rated at 1,000 liters/hour running 6 peak sun hours gives 6,000 liters/day. So you need about 9 such pumps, or a larger pump. For 55,000 liters/day, you need a pump that delivers about 9,200 liters/hour over 6 hours. That is a 3-4 HP pump. Write down your daily demand. It is the first number for sizing panels, pump, and tank. Also consider peak demand: if you irrigate only 3 days a week, daily demand during those days is higher. Design for the peak day.

lessons.title: Safety and Environmental Considerations
lessons.body:
Solar pumping is safe, but you must respect electricity, water, and the environment. This lesson covers key safety and environmental rules.

Electrical safety: Solar panels produce DC electricity whenever exposed to light. Cover panels with a cloth before wiring to prevent shock. Use properly rated cables and connectors. DC arcs are dangerousânever disconnect under load. Install a DC circuit breaker between panels and controller. Ground the panel frames and controller. If you use AC pumps, ensure the inverter is grounded and protected by an RCD (Residual Current Device). Keep children away from the array and controller.

Water safety: Dams can be deep and have soft banks. Never work alone near water. Wear a life jacket if you go in. Use a rope to secure yourself. When installing a submersible pump, use a tripod or winchâdo not lift by hand. Ensure the pump is tied with a safety rope so you can retrieve it. Avoid pumping near the dam wall to prevent erosion. Place the intake on a stand or float to avoid sucking mud.

Environmental considerations: Do not pump the dam below its ecological reserve. Leave at least 30% of volume for fish, wildlife, and downstream users. In some countries, this is law. Check with your local water authority. Avoid fuel spillsâsolar has none. But batteries (if used) contain lead and acid. Recycle them properly. Do not dump old panels; they contain silicon and metals that can be recycled. Use biodegradable lubricants for pumps if possible.

Social considerations: Water is shared. Before installing a pump, talk to neighbors and local leaders. Agree on water allocation. A solar pump can increase water access, but it can also cause conflict if one farmer takes too much. Form a water user association. Keep records of pumping hours and volumes. Train at least two people to operate and maintain the system. Keep a spare controller and pump on site if possible.

Finally, protect your investment: fence the solar array, lock the controller box, and insure the system if available. With these precautions, solar pumping for dams is safe, clean, and sustainable.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of solar pumps over diesel pumps for dam applications?
options: C) They have no fuel cost
D) They work at night without batteries
quiz.explanation: Solar pumps use sunlight, so there is no fuel cost, unlike diesel pumps.

quiz.q: Which component matches the solar panel output to the pump?
quiz.explanation: The controller or inverter regulates voltage and current to protect and power the pump.

quiz.q: What is the recommended minimum water level to leave in a dam?
quiz.explanation: Leave at least 30% for ecological and emergency use.

quiz.q: How many peak sun hours does most of Africa receive per day?
quiz.explanation: Most of Africa gets 4 to 6 peak sun hours daily, which is ideal for solar pumping.

quiz.q: What does 'head' refer to in pump sizing?
options: A) The depth of the dam
B) The vertical distance water must be lifted plus friction loss
C) The width of the pipe
D) The number of solar panels
quiz.explanation: Head is total lift: vertical elevation plus friction losses in pipes.

quiz.q: Which pump type is best for a deep dam?
quiz.explanation: Submersible pumps are placed in the water and can lift from deep sources without suction limits.

quiz.q: What is a common configuration for dam solar pumping?
quiz.explanation: Direct-coupled with a storage tank is common because it avoids batteries and pumps during sunny hours.

quiz.q: How much water does a 1 HP solar pump typically lift to 10 meters head per day?
quiz.explanation: A 1 HP pump can lift about 10,000 liters per day to 10 meters head under good sun.

quiz.q: What is the first step in site assessment?
options: B) Measure dam layout and head
quiz.explanation: You must map the dam, measure distance and elevation before sizing any equipment.

quiz.q: How do you calculate total head?
options: B) Vertical lift plus friction loss
quiz.explanation: Total head = vertical elevation difference + friction losses from pipe length and fittings.

quiz.q: For every 100m of pipe, how much extra head should you add for friction?
quiz.explanation: A rough rule is 1m of head per 100m of pipe to account for friction.

quiz.q: What tool can measure elevation difference?
options: B) Clinometer or smartphone level app
quiz.explanation: A clinometer or level app measures vertical angles to calculate elevation change.

quiz.q: What does a float switch do?
options: B) Stops pump when tank is full or dam is low
quiz.explanation: Float switches automatically control pump operation based on water level.

quiz.q: How much water does one cow drink per day?
quiz.explanation: Cattle need about 40-50 liters of water daily.

quiz.q: For 0.5 hectare of tomatoes needing 7 mm/day, what is the daily water demand before losses?
quiz.explanation: 0.5 ha * 7 mm * 10,000 L/mm/ha = 35,000 liters per day.

quiz.q: Why add 20% to irrigation water demand?
options: A) For evaporation and distribution losses
quiz.explanation: Adding 20% accounts for evaporation, seepage, and uneven application.

quiz.q: What is the daily domestic water need for 100 people at 20 liters each?
quiz.explanation: 100 people * 20 liters = 2,000 liters per day.

quiz.q: If total daily demand is 55,000 liters, and you have 6 peak sun hours, what pump flow rate is needed?
quiz.explanation: 55,000 liters / 6 hours = about 9,200 liters per hour.

quiz.q: What safety device should be used before wiring solar panels?
quiz.explanation: Covering panels stops electricity production, preventing shock during wiring.

quiz.q: Why should you not pump a dam below 30%?
options: A) To protect fish and downstream users
quiz.explanation: Leaving 30% maintains ecological balance and water for emergencies.

quiz.q: What is a risk of using a diesel pump near a dam?
options: A) Fuel spill harming water quality
quiz.explanation: Diesel spills can contaminate dam water, harming livestock and fish.

quiz.q: How should you dispose of old batteries?
quiz.explanation: Batteries contain lead and acid; they must be recycled to prevent pollution.

quiz.q: What is a simple way to check solar potential without tools?
quiz.explanation: A shadow shorter than 1m from a 1m stick at noon indicates good sun.

quiz.q: Why fence a solar array?
options: A) To prevent theft and animal damage
quiz.explanation: Fencing protects panels from theft and livestock damage.

quiz.q: What is the role of a non-return valve?
quiz.explanation: A non-return valve stops water from flowing back into the dam when pump stops.

quiz.q: Which pipe material is commonly used for solar pump systems?
quiz.explanation: PVC and HDPE are cheap, durable, and easy to install for water piping.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a storage tank in a solar pump system?
options: A) Store water for use when sun is not shining
quiz.explanation: A tank stores water pumped during sunny hours for later use.

quiz.q: How many liters per day does a 300W solar panel system typically pump?
quiz.explanation: A 300W system can pump about 5,000 liters per day under good sun.

quiz.q: What should you do before installing a pump in a shared dam?
options: A) Talk to neighbors and local leaders
quiz.explanation: Community agreement prevents conflicts over water use.

quiz.q: What is the recommended tilt for solar panels in Zambia (15Â°S)?
quiz.explanation: In southern hemisphere, tilt panels north at angle equal to latitude.
